compiled_prompt:
[TASK: ARCHITECTURAL RELIGHTING & STATIC RECONSTRUCTION]
Transform the reference photogrammetry plate into a razor-sharp, photorealistic architectural image.
Keep the reference plate's exact composition: every edge, horizon line, and object position stays where it is.

MANDATORY TRANSFORMATION RULES:
1. PLANAR RECTIFICATION & GEOMETRY LOCK: Treat the reference image as an immutable spatial coordinate frame. Eliminate all 3D mesh polygon wobble, melted facades, and distorted rooflines. Plumb all vertical walls to true gravity vertical. Render the specific materials, coursing, window types, and roof forms named in the SCENE section below with sharp, correct detail.
2. STATIC DECLUTTERING (MANDATORY): COMPLETELY ERASE all transient vehicles, parked cars, delivery vans, pedestrians, and temporary street clutter from the seed image. Repaint the ground plane with the authentic surfacing, kerbs, and pavement named in the SCENE section below.
3. BOTANICAL PHENOLOGY & CANOPY INTEGRITY: Overwrite all raw 3D mesh blob foliage with authentic seasonal canopy structures matching the target date. Zero green summer foliage during dormant/autumn/winter periods:
   Bordering parkland features mature *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore) and *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime). Late September phenology: full canopy volumes exhibiting early autumn senescence, chlorotic margin yellowing, and minor crown defoliation.
4. OPTICAL DEPTH: Sharp focus across the entire frame, near to far. No blur, no depth-of-field falloff, no vignetting.

[SOLAR & ATMOSPHERIC LIGHTING OVERRIDE]
SOLAR RELIGHTING DIRECTIVE (4500K Late afternoon raking sunlight with warm golden highlights):
- SUN POSITION IN SCREEN SPACE: Sun is ahead and to the RIGHT, in the upper-right background (True Azimuth 243.4°, Elevation 17.1°).
- FACADE ILLUMINATION: all camera-facing facades are in shadow, reading as backlit silhouettes with a bright rim along their sunward edges; right-facing walls are brightly lit and left-facing walls are in deep shadow.
- CAST SHADOW DIRECTION: cast shadows project diagonally toward the camera and to the lower-LEFT.
- CAST SHADOW LENGTH: Every cast shadow is 3.3 times as long as the height of the object casting it. A 100 m tower casts a 326 m shadow. Apply this ratio to every object in the scene.
- SHADOW OVERWRITE RULE: MANDATORY: Erase every cast shadow present in the reference plate before relighting. Render all previously shadowed ground and facades as if that shadow never existed, then cast entirely new shadows so that cast shadows project diagonally toward the camera and to the lower-LEFT. Every shadow must be angled toward the LEFT; a shadow running straight up or straight down the frame is wrong. Do not retain, tint, or reuse any shadow from the reference plate.
- WEATHER/SKY: Crisp clear sky with direct solar exposure.

[SCENE GEOMETRY & AUTHENTIC LITHICS]
Edinburgh Charlotte Square western elevation centered on West Register House. Monumental neo-classical church facade constructed in finely dressed pale buff Craigleith sandstone ashlar, featuring a colossal stepped Ionic portico beneath a square base, circular peristyle drum, and prominent hemispherical dome clad in weathered copper with turquoise-green verdigris patination, topped by a stone lantern. Flanking unified Georgian residential terraces designed by Robert Adam, rising three storeys above rusticated ground-floor basements with sunken lightwells fronted by black cast-iron spearhead railings. Regular fenestration composed of timber 6-over-6 sash-and-case windows set into moulded stone architraves, topped by continuous moulded entablatures, mutule cornices, and rooftop parapet balustrades. Mansard and pitched roofs clad in dark grey Scottish Ballachulish slates with dressed stone chimney stacks. Ground plane paved in broad split Caithness stone flagstones, edged by dressed whinstone kerbs and a clean asphalt carriageway. To the lateral garden boundary, mature Tilia cordata and Acer pseudoplatanus display early autumn phenology with dense canopies exhibiting chlorotic edge yellowing and selective foliage thinning. Historic coal-smoke patination and localized sulfate crusting across sandstone friezes.
